desktopInput.mouse: relative head look; client-bound right-hand aim in menu or while right mouse is held
desktopInput.menu: M and Esc share Quick Menu state; left hand remains raised until closed; Tab untouched
desktopInput.use: left click or held trigger drag
desktopInput.grab: middle mouse only; right mouse pointer sends no Grip
desktopInput.chat: Y opens, Enter sends while typing, Esc cancels while typing

locomotion.crouch: C toggles crouch; repeat to stand
locomotion.prone: Z toggles prone; repeat to stand; selecting another posture replaces the current posture

controllerMapping.run: left joystick/thumbstick click; app binding dependent
controllerMapping.menu: one verified Boolean click: left y, left b, right b, left application_menu in preference order
controllerMapping.system: neutral in desktop mode; never synthesize dashboard button

handPresets: left menu hand and right pointer (preset 3)
limitations: Profile declares shipped mappings; actual bindings must be validated on the active controller.
Menu and right-held pointer use relative mouse hand aim; pixel-perfect mirror clicking is unavailable.
Installed default Touch bindings map left Y/right B clicks to Quick Menu and separate their touch gesture actions; stored bindings do not prove the current app binding.
VRChat must already use SteamVR VR rendering; native desktop sessions cannot be converted.
Persistent-HMD Virtual Desktop late-attachment and connected-start display trials failed and were rolled back; headset-free startup remains unimplemented.
Disable VRChat Freeze Tracking on Disconnect for Desktop body fallback. VD body fallback and physical return passed; other calibration/providers remain unverified.
Cursor hiding, wrist aiming and latched locomotion animation need repaired-build live verification; face/eye channels remain untested.
evidence: Controlled-scene headset tests passed; original menu closure and later VRChat cursor/hands/menu/posture F3 failed. Replacement controls are software-tested and await live retest; public model components do not prove VRChat's consumed pointer component.
